sections.h2: Hospitals drew far less foreign capital than pharmaceuticals despite an open route

chart.title: Hospitals drew $8.89 billion since 2000, well under pharma's $21.6 billion
chart.sub: Cumulative FDI equity inflow, April 2000 to June 2023, US$ million.
chart.source: DPIIT consolidated FDI sector-wise tables, Jan 2000 to Jun 2023.

sections.means: Hospitals have been on the automatic route with 100 per cent foreign ownership since 2000, so policy has not been the constraint.
sections.todo: Check the sector's FDI tables in each new DPIIT fact sheet before treating inflow as a trend.

sections.h2: Recent deals buy existing hospital chains rather than building new beds

events: TPG/GIC take a majority of Asian Institute of Nephrology & Urology for ₹600 crore
Blackstone takes 72.5% of Quality Care India, which acquires about 80% of KIMS Health for ₹3,300 crore
KKR buys full ownership of Medicover's Indian hospitals for $1.39bn
Manipal takes a majority of Sahyadri Hospitals for ₹6,300–6,400 crore

sections.means: Every large deal in this list changes the owner of beds that already existed, and none adds a new hospital.
sections.todo: Ask whether any new bed capacity is foreign-financed before counting these deals as expansion.

sections.h2: India's bed ratio sits well below the world and OECD averages

chart.title: India's 1.59 beds per 1,000 is under half the world average of 3.29
chart.source: World Bank series SH.MED.BEDS.ZS (WHO data); government-bed figure from The South First.

sections.means: Neither the bed ratio nor the shortfall figures have moved because of foreign capital, since the deals add no beds.
sections.todo: Pull a sourced, current bed-per-1,000 figure from the government before relying on the 1.4 or 3.5 numbers.
